summary: Honest limits: CC&Rs/declarations are private instruments recorded with the county clerk/recorder; few counties offer free bulk text. Per house a user can search the recorder by subdivision or developer name, read the title commitment or HOA resale certificate, or ask the HOA (most states grant owner record-access).

Texas Property Code ch. 209 (Residential Property Owners Protection Act): notice-and-cure before fines or suits, owner records access (209.005), open board meetings, management certificate (209.004), foreclosure limits. Chapter 82 governs condominiums.

Texas Property Code ch. 202 limits what deed restrictions/HOAs may ban: drought-resistant landscaping, rain barrels, composting (202.007), solar devices (202.010), impact-resistant/energy roofing (202.011), flags (202.012), religious items (202.018), standby generators (202.019), pool enclosures (202.022), security measures (202.023). Reasonable placement rules still allowed.

Rentals/STR: Texas HOAs can restrict leasing or short-term rentals when the recorded declaration clearly does; the Texas Supreme Court (Tarr v. Timberwood Park, 2018) held a generic residential-use covenant did not by itself bar STRs. No specific state HOA override found for ADUs or EV chargers.

Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act (CCIOA, C.R.S. 38-33.3): association powers, owner records access (38-33.3-317), collections and dispute rules. Protects flags/signs, drought-tolerant landscaping (no nonfunctional-turf mandates), EV chargers, solar (38-30-168) and, per HB24-1152, ADUs where locally allowed. Rental limits possible via declaration.

Minnesota Common Interest Ownership Act, ch. 515B: declaration limits, owner rights, association records (515B.3-118). Separate statutes void HOA/deed bans on flag display (500.215), solar energy systems (500.216, reasonable restrictions allowed) and certain child care (500.217). Leasing limits allowed if in the declaration.

Ohio Revised Code ch. 5312 (planned communities/HOAs) and ch. 5311 (condominiums): association powers, assessments, fines after notice and hearing, owner records inspection. Flag protections exist; no broad Ohio HOA override for solar or ADUs found (verify).

RSMo 442.404: HOAs may not prohibit political signs (reasonable rules allowed), solar panels (with exceptions and placement rules), for-sale signs, and some chicken-keeping. Missouri Uniform Condominium Act is ch. 448. No general records statute for non-condo HOAs found.

Oklahoma has no comprehensive HOA act; condos fall under the Unit Ownership Estate Act (60 O.S. 501 et seq.); subdivision HOAs rely on recorded covenants and nonprofit-corporation law. Specific flag/solar protections not confirmed.

Alabama Homeowners' Association Act (Code of Ala. 35-20-1 et seq., 2015) mainly covers HOAs formed after 1 Jan 2016 (older ones may opt in): governance, fines, records. Condos: Alabama Uniform Condominium Act (35-8A). Specific solar/flag protections not confirmed.

Federal overrides on HOAs: Freedom to Display the American Flag Act (2005); FCC OTARD rule (47 CFR 1.4000) limiting HOA bans on satellite dishes/small antennas; Fair Housing Act bars discriminatory covenants (racial covenants unenforceable).

Zoning 'family' definition plus Housing Maintenance Code (Title 12, ch. 244) floor-area occupancy rules. ADUs allowed citywide (since 2014; 2040 plan allows up to 3 units per lot). Sheds, tents, RVs are not legal dwellings. Unrelated-adult cap varies by district (historically 3-5) - verify current text.

Legislative Code ch. 34 (minimum property standards) governs sleeping-room size and occupancy; zoning code (Title VIII) defines family. ADUs allowed citywide since 2018, later liberalised. RV/shed/tent dwelling not allowed. Unrelated-adult cap (around 4) - verify.

Dallas Development Code (ch. 51A) defines 'family' (commonly cited: up to 4 unrelated); Minimum Housing Standards (ch. 27) set space per occupant. Additional dwelling units in single-family districts generally need a Board of Adjustment special exception. RV/shed living not allowed.

Land Development Code (Title 25) residential occupancy limit (4-6 unrelated adults depending on district/date - verify). HOME amendments (2023-24) allow up to 3 units on a single-family lot and smaller lots. Tiny homes on wheels/RVs only in RV parks or approved communities.

Denver Zoning Code group-living update (2021) let households include up to 5 unrelated adults plus relatives; Colorado HB24-1007 now bars relationship-based caps. ADUs allowed citywide (2023 update; state HB24-1152). Tiny-home villages only via special/temporary permits; RV/tent dwelling on lots not allowed.

Boulder historically capped unrelated occupants at 3-4; after HB24-1007 the city moved to life-safety/size-based limits (verify ordinance). ADUs allowed by right with owner-occupancy relaxed (2024). Rental licensing (B.R.C. 10-3) records occupancy. Sheds/RVs are not dwellings.

Columbus Zoning Code (Title 33) 'family' with an unrelated-person limit (verify, commonly 3-4); Housing Code (Title 45) sets space per occupant. 'Zone In' rewrite (2025-26) expands ADU and missing-middle options - check adopted status. RV/tent/shed living not allowed.

Cincinnati Zoning Code (Title XIV) family definition (unrelated cap - verify, commonly 4); ADUs allowed in single-family districts and expanded by Connected Communities (2024). Housing code sets occupancy. RV/tent/shed living not allowed.

Tulsa Zoning Code: household definition and detached accessory dwelling units (allowed in many RS districts, some by special exception - verify). City adopts a property maintenance code. RV/shed living not allowed. Unrelated-person cap not confirmed.

Zoning & Development Code (ch. 88) defines household; ADUs broadened by recent amendments (verify scope). Property maintenance code (ch. 56) governs sleeping-room occupancy. RV/tent/shed living not allowed.

Huntsville Zoning Ordinance defines family; accessory dwellings limited (guest houses often without separate kitchen or rental - verify). Adopted IPMC/IRC govern sleeping rooms and egress. RV/shed living not allowed.

Birmingham Zoning Ordinance defines family and limits accessory dwellings (verify). Adopted building and property maintenance codes govern occupancy and egress. RV/shed/tent living not allowed on residential lots.

Most of our cities adopt ICC model codes with local amendments: the IPMC sets minimum sleeping-room floor area (one occupant, plus extra per added occupant) and space per occupant; IRC R310 requires an emergency escape opening in every sleeping room, including basements. Bunk beds are not separately regulated - occupancy counts people, not beds.

Permanent living in sheds/accessory structures, tents on private lots, or RVs/tiny homes on wheels is not allowed in any of the 12 cities (not a dwelling unit under zoning/building codes). Narrow exceptions: short guest RV stays, construction/disaster occupancy, and sanctioned tiny-home villages (e.g., Denver, Austin).

Colorado HB24-1007 (2024) bars local governments from limiting residential occupancy based on familial relationship; occupancy limits must rest on health and safety standards. Affects Denver and Boulder.

Colorado HB24-1152 (2024): covered urban jurisdictions must allow one ADU by right on single-unit lots (deadline mid-2025), without owner-occupancy mandates and with limited parking rules; also limits HOA prohibitions on ADUs.

Texas SB 840 (89th Leg., effective 1 Sep 2025): larger cities must allow multifamily/mixed-use by right on many commercially zoned sites and commercial-to-residential conversions. Relevant to co-living and to church-owned commercial parcels.

Rooming/boarding houses and co-living are usually separate uses (rooming house, group living) limited to specific zones and often needing rental or lodging licences; renting rooms beyond the household cap in single-family zones is generally a violation. Check each city's use table.

RLUIPA (42 U.S.C. 2000cc): land-use rules may not substantially burden religious exercise unless the least restrictive means to a compelling interest; religious assemblies must get equal terms with secular assemblies and cannot be totally or unreasonably excluded. DOJ enforces.

Colorado HB25-1169 'Housing Developments on Faith and Educational Land' (YIGBY) would have required by-right housing on faith/school land from end-2026; reported lost in the Senate (May 2025). No enacted Colorado YIGBY law found.
Texas SB 854 (89th Leg.) would have allowed multifamily/mixed-use by right on religious land; it died in the Senate (last action 3 Apr 2025). Churches can still use SB 840 on commercially zoned land.

Minnesota SF 4915 'Yes in God's Back Yard (YIGBY) Housing Act' introduced 26 Mar 2026 and referred to State and Local Government committee only - not enacted. Housing on church land still needs local zoning approval.
No enacted state YIGBY law found for Ohio, Oklahoma, Missouri or Alabama (searches Nov 2026). Local zoning plus RLUIPA governs.

Typical treatment: religious assembly is permitted or conditional in most residential and commercial districts (often conditional in single-family zones, with parking/site rules); accessory shelters, schools and parsonages vary. Housing on church land generally needs rezoning/PUD or uses general multi-unit rules (e.g., Austin HOME, Minneapolis 3-unit). Verify per use table.
